source_title: Judge Again Tosses Out Donald Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit Against The Wall Street Journal Over Its Reporting On Jeffrey Epstein Birthday Letter

UPDATED: A federal judge has again dismissed Donald Trump ‘s $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over its reporting on a letter sent to Jeffrey Epstein for his birthday in 2003.
U.S. District Judge Darrin P. Gayles wrote in his opinion that Trump’s lawsuit “falls short of pleading actual malice. Indeed, the allegations regarding malice are conclusory, vague, sometimes inconsistent with the Article, and often irrelevant to whether Defendants knew or should have known that the statements in the Article were purportedly false.”
Trump sued the Journal as well as a series of other defendants, including Rupert Murdoch, after it published an article in July, 2025 reporting on the contents of a bawdy letter bearing Trump’s name and included in a “birthday book” compiled for Epstein’s 50th birthday. In its story, the Journal reported that the letter “contains several lines of typewritten text framed by the outline of a naked woman, which appears to be hand-drawn with a heavy marker,” adding that a “pair of small arcs denotes the woman’s breasts, and the future president’s signature is a squiggly ‘Donald’ below her waist, mimicking pubic hair.” Watch on Deadline
Trump has claimed that he did not compose the letter. The article did include Trump’s denial and that he was preparing to sue. Also named in the lawsuit were parent Dow Jones, News Corp. CEO Robert Thomson and reporters Khadeeja Safdar and Joseph Palazzo.
The judge previously tossed out Trump’s case, concluding that it failed to allege actual malice, but allowed it to be amended. The judge’s latest ruling, though, is with prejudice, meaning the same claim cannot be refiled.
A spokesman for the president’s legal team said the president “will continue to press forward in his powerhouse lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and all of the other defendants. The President will continue to hold those who mislead the American People with Fake News and smears accountable for their actions.”
A spokesperson for Dow Jones said, “We’re pleased with the court’s decision.”
In his opinion , the judge opened with a quote from Justice Louis Brandeis in his concurring opinion in New York Times vs. Sullivan, the landmark 1964 Supreme Court ruling that set the precedent for public figures seeking defamation claims. It set the standard that public figures had to prove actual malice, or show that a media outlet published a story with knowledge that it was false or that it was done with reckless disregard for the truth.
Brandeis wrote, “Those who won our independence believed … that public discussion is a political duty; and that this should be a fundamental principle of the American government.”
In Trump’s revised lawsuit, his attorneys claimed that the Journal reporters “did not have access to any such letter when the Article was published, which is a fact because no authentic letter or drawing exists.” They claimed the journalists “concocted this story to malign President Trump’s character and integrity, and to deceptively portray him in a false light.”
The House Oversight Committee later released documents that included a letter matching the Journal‘s description.
Trump’s amended lawsuit pointed to his denials and to statements from Ghislaine Maxwell, the Epstein associate who is currently serving a sentence for her role in trafficking of underage girls. The lawsuit noted that, in an interview with then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche and other DOJ officials later in July of 2025, Maxwell had stated that she did not remember submitting a Trump letter for Epstein’s birthday. The Journal story noted that they attempted to reach her, but she did not respond to a request for an interview, and her attorney did not address the letter.
The judge declined to determine whether Trump was the author of the letter, whether the statements in the article are true, and that they were not defamatory. But he rejected Trump’s argument that the Journal’s publication of the story, despite his denials, was evidence of actual malice.
The judge wrote, “In effect, President Trump argues that once he declared the Letter a ‘fake,’ Defendants should have disregarded everything else they learned in their investigation and not published the story. But that is not what the actual malice standard requires and runs afoul of the First Amendment.”
The judge added that “were that the law, any time a public figure or his team denies an accusation, journalists would be immediately blocked from publishing negative or contradictory press.”
The judge also rejected Trump’s claim that the Journal’s investigation of the letter was inadequate, noting that “a failure to investigate, without more, does not establish actual malice.” But the judge also noted that the Journal reached out to a number of officials, including others named in the Epstein birthday book. Gayles also wrote that the Trump lawsuit references to Maxwell are a “red herring” and do not establish that the Journal reporters harbored “serious doubts” over the story.
The judge wrote that the Journal could file a motion to collect attorneys’ fees.

एक संघीय न्यायाधीश ने जेफरी एपस्टीन को 2003 में भेजे गए जन्मदिन के पत्र की रिपोर्टिंग को लेकर द वॉल स्ट्रीट जर्नल के खिलाफ डोनाल्ड ट्रंप के 10 अरब डॉलर के मानहानि मुकदमे को खारिज कर दिया है। अमेरिकी जिला न्यायाधीश डैरिन पी. गेलेस ने फैसला सुनाया कि यह मुकदमा वास्तविक दुर्भावना (actual malice) को पर्याप्त रूप से साबित करने में विफल रहा, और इस बार यह फैसला मुकदमे को दोबारा दाखिल करने के अधिकार के बिना (with prejudice) दिया गया है।

### मुकदमे की पृष्ठभूमि

यह कानूनी कार्रवाई जुलाई 2025 में जर्नल द्वारा प्रकाशित एक लेख के बाद शुरू हुई थी, जिसमें एपस्टीन के 50वें जन्मदिन के लिए संकलित एक जन्मदिन की किताब में शामिल एक पत्र का विवरण दिया गया था। प्रकाशन ने बताया था कि पत्र में एक नग्न महिला की रूपरेखा के भीतर टाइप किया गया पाठ था, जिसके साथ एक हस्ताक्षर भी था। ट्रंप ने लगातार इस पत्र को लिखने से इनकार किया है, और मूल लेख में उनके खंडन तथा मुकदमे की तैयारी की बात शामिल थी। इस मुकदमे में जर्नल, उसकी मूल कंपनी डॉव जोन्स, न्यूज कॉर्प के सीईओ रॉबर्ट थॉमसन और संवाददाताओं खादीजा सफदर और जोसेफ पलाज्जो को नामजद किया गया था।

### अदालत के निष्कर्ष और कानूनी मानक

न्यायाधीश गेलेस ने पहले भी इस मामले को खारिज कर दिया था लेकिन संशोधन की अनुमति दी थी, हालांकि ताजा फैसला अंतिम है। अपने फैसले में, न्यायाधीश ने 1964 के सुप्रीम कोर्ट के ऐतिहासिक फैसले *न्यू यॉर्क टाइम्स बनाम सुलिवन* का हवाला दिया, जिसमें यह कड़ा कानूनी मानक तय किया गया था कि सार्वजनिक हस्तियों को मानहानि साबित करने के लिए वास्तविक दुर्भावना को साबित करना होगा।

* अदालत ने नोट किया कि दुर्भावना के संबंध में ट्रंप के आरोप निष्कर्षपूर्ण और अस्पष्ट थे।
* न्यायाधीश ने इस तर्क को खारिज कर दिया कि केवल इसलिए कि कोई सार्वजनिक हस्ती दावों से इनकार करती है, पत्रकारों को कहानी प्रकाशित करना बंद कर देना चाहिए।
* फैसले में कहा गया कि जांच की कमी मात्र से वास्तविक दुर्भावना साबित नहीं होती है।

### प्रतिक्रियाएं और व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ

डॉव जोन्स के एक प्रवक्ता ने कहा कि कंपनी अदालत के फैसले से संतुष्ट है। इस बीच, ट्रंप की कानूनी टीम के एक प्रतिनिधि ने संकेत दिया कि राष्ट्रपति मुकदमे को आगे बढ़ाएंगे और जनता को गुमराह करने वालों को जवाबदेह ठहराएंगे। अदालत ने यह भी संकेत दिया कि प्रतिवादी वकीलों की फीस वसूलने के लिए प्रस्ताव दायर कर सकते हैं। सत्यापन के लिए संबंधित संघीय अदालत के रिकॉर्ड देखे जा सकते हैं।

en_body:
A federal judge has dismissed Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal with prejudice over its reporting regarding a 2003 birthday letter sent to Jeffrey Epstein. U.S. District Judge Darrin P. Gayles ruled that the lawsuit failed to adequately plead actual malice, marking the final dismissal of the case.

### Background of the Lawsuit

The legal action followed a July 2025 article published by the Journal detailing a bawdy letter included in a birthday book compiled for Epstein's 50th birthday. The publication described the letter as containing typewritten text framed by the outline of a naked woman, accompanied by a signature resembling Trump's name. Trump consistently denied composing the letter, and the original article included his denials alongside plans to sue. The lawsuit named the Journal, parent company Dow Jones, News Corp. CEO Robert Thomson, and reporters Khadeeja Safdar and Joseph Palazzo.

### Court Findings and Legal Standards

Judge Gayles previously dismissed the case with leave to amend, but the latest ruling is with prejudice, preventing the claim from being refiled. In his opinion, the judge cited the landmark 1964 Supreme Court ruling *New York Times vs. Sullivan*, emphasizing the strict legal standard that public figures must prove actual malice—meaning the publisher knew the statement was false or acted with reckless disregard for the truth.

* The court noted that Trump's allegations regarding malice were conclusory, vague, and inconsistent.
* The judge rejected the argument that journalists must drop a story simply because a public figure denies the claims.
* The ruling stated that a failure to investigate, without more, does not establish actual malice.

### Responses and Practical Implications

A spokesperson for Dow Jones stated that the company is pleased with the court's decision. Meanwhile, a representative for Trump's legal team indicated that the president intends to press forward with the lawsuit and hold those accountable for misleading the public. The court also indicated that the defendants could file a motion to collect attorneys' fees. Observers and legal scholars can review the complete judicial opinion through federal court electronic records (PACER) using the specific district court docket information for verification.
